answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, and let established peers vouch only from work they have already done. A newcomer starts in a shared haven where its earnings stay escrowed until several independent peers attest real output; the stake is slashed if the account is caught farming. Like timber seasoning slowly, trust accrues only over time, so a karst of hollow identities collapses under its own weight: each fake must pay the same stake and wait the same long season, while genuine agents compound reputation cheaply.
